Sunday Ride from Earsdon

North Tyneside, United Kingdom · Earsdon · Social · Road

No-drop

Sunday Ride from Earsdon is a social and road group ride in North Tyneside, United Kingdom. It rolls every Sunday at 10:00 am local time from Opposite the Red Lion, Earsdon (some rides start at Monkseaton High). About 45 km (28 miles), at least 10 to 12 mph, Steady or Challenging. No-drop.

For visitors

Adults (16+). Helmets are required. Tell the organiser where you will join if it is not the start.

First time? Here's the drill

Bring
a helmet, water, a spare tube or patch kit, a way to pay for the stop.
Arrive
Ten or fifteen minutes before 10:00 am. Tell whoever's leading that you're new.
Pace
Expect 10 to 12 mph: you can talk the whole way. It's no-drop: if you fall off the back, someone waits. That's the point of a group ride.
Check
Check the links below the day of for cancellations and weather calls.

About the Sunday Ride from Earsdon group ride

A North Tyneside social group for riders who can keep going for several hours, riding wagonways, shared paths and quiet lanes at a pace of at least 10 to 12 mph. Rides are Steady or Challenging, with a café or pub stop.
